findings.note: Documentation and spec both say epic-ready renders the literal string "not sharded", but the shipped context pack renders a different sentence. INSTALL.md:128 and docs/quickstart.md:62 - corrected on this same branch - state 'epic-ready renders "not sharded"', and the 0.8.3 spec section 9 specifies that ShardPlanMarkdown (which emits "## Context Shard Plan\n\nNot sharded.", contextprofile/shards.go:266) does the rendering at epicready/review.go:500. The diff instead hard-codes "Sharding is not applied to epic-ready reviews; see the child task-done and pr-ready packs." An operator or agent grepping an epic-ready pack for the documented phrase finds nothing, and hard-coding the section bypasses the shared renderer, so a future heading change in contextprofile silently diverges here. No test or shell test asserts either string (grep over *_test.go and tests/**.sh finds no assertion of the epic-ready shard-plan section), so nothing pins the wording either way.

findings.note: The snapshot loop can panic instead of reporting drift, and scanner errors are silently ignored. TestGoldenPrefixes drives the index i from the lines of testdata/golden-snapshots.jsonl but slices stored, which comes from testdata/golden-log.jsonl: if the snapshots file ever holds more lines than the log (a hand edit, a partially written regeneration, or a log line above MaxLine that makes bufio.Scanner stop early), stored[:i+1] panics with index out of range before the trailing `i != len(stored)` check - which only catches the too-few direction - can report anything. Neither sc.Err() nor ws.Err() is checked, so a scanner error is indistinguishable from a short file. Test-only, and both goldens are consistent today (24 lines each), but the failure mode of a regression fixture should be a readable diff, not a panic.

findings.note: shellcheck is the one tool in this workflow that is not pinned, in a repository whose own workflows argue for pinning. Every action is pinned by SHA and golangci-lint is pinned to v2.13.1, while gtg.yml:38-41 pins gtg with an explicit comment that an unpinned release 'could change what the gate means without a change in this repository'. `sudo apt-get install -y -qq shellcheck` takes whatever the runner image's apt index offers, so a distro bump can turn a green branch red with no repo change - the same failure the other pins exist to prevent. The install is also redundant: the ubuntu-latest image ships ShellCheck, so the step adds an apt round trip and a network failure mode for a binary that is already present.

evidence.note: unpinned apt install of shellcheck
golangci-lint action pinned by SHA and version v2.13.1 in the very next step
sibling workflow pins gtg==0.10.0 with a comment justifying exactly this discipline

findings.note: The shellcheck invocation has no empty-input guard: `find ... -print0 | xargs -0 shellcheck -x` runs shellcheck with no file arguments when find matches nothing, and shellcheck then exits nonzero with a usage error, failing the gate for a reason that has nothing to do with the shell scripts. GNU xargs needs -r/--no-run-if-empty for this. Latent today (38 .sh files match), but it turns 'the suite moved under an excluded path' into a confusing red build rather than a no-op. Related: the pipeline's exit status is xargs's, so a find failure would be masked - only the xargs status reaches the step.

evidence.note: xargs -0 shellcheck -x with no -r and no pipefail
